clue.text: For each one getting sad when husband's gone travelling

parts.note: per is Latin for 'for each', as in per head
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: gone says the husband's letter has left the word for sad

parts.note: pathetic means pitiful, sad
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Someone becomes miserable while their husband is away on a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Peripatetic describes someone who moves from place to place, a synonym of wandering about.

clue.text: Wire tensioner in piano, for example

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
eg, exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Something that tightens strings in a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; the piano also supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuning peg is turned to adjust the tension of a stringed instrument's wires.

clue.text: Become very warm right on top of kiln

indicators.note: in a down clue, on top of puts the right letter above the kiln

parts.note: an oast is a kiln for drying hops

explanation.surface: Things heat up a great deal just above the kiln.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast is informally to become uncomfortably hot, as in sunbathing.

clue.text: Preparing for firing mostly proper porcelain

indicators.note: mostly says the proper word loses its last letter

parts.note: prim means proper, prudish
Ming is fine Chinese porcelain

explanation.surface: Getting ceramic ware ready for the kiln, mostly fine porcelain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firing' suggests a kiln, but the definition is about readying a gun: priming loads the charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Priming a gun means preparing its charge so that it can be fired.

clue.text: Solvent in can, good for fixing in position

indicators.note: in puts the solvent inside the can

parts.note: a tin is a can
ether is an organic solvent

explanation.surface: A solvent kept in a tin is good for holding something in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Tethering is tying something with a rope so it stays fixed where it is.

clue.text: The heart's rhythm of beating, primarily

definitions.text: The heart's rhythm of beating, primarily

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of each word in the clue

explanation.surface: The basic pulse of the heart beating.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a strong regular pulse, like a heartbeat.

clue.text: One's needing a last alcoholic drink

definitions.meaning: a shoemaker works on a last, a foot-shaped block
a cocktail of wine or sherry with sugar, citrus and ice

explanation.surface: Someone who desperately needs one final drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' looks like 'final'; it is the cobbler's foot-shaped mould.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoe mender uses a last; a sherry mixed with fruit and ice also bears the name.

clue.text: Source of wine some purchasers sent back

indicators.note: sent back means the hidden run is read right to left
some means only part of the word purchasers is used

explanation.surface: A wine supply that some buyers returned to the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes URC from inside 'purchasers'; 'sent back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A cru is a vineyard or growth producing wine of a recognised quality, so it is where wine comes from.

clue.text: Coalition partner getting one up on a Liberal? Happening all the time

parts.note: Con, a Conservative, partner in a coalition

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the one word is read upwards, reversed

parts.note: a unit is one

explanation.surface: In a coalition, the Conservative partner always gets one over on the Liberal.
explanation.definitionFit: Continual means recurring constantly, without stopping.

clue.text: Non-stop fun!

parts.note: read as wordplay, the letters UN F with 'altering' as an instruction rearrange into the word fun

explanation.surface: An exclamation of endless enjoyment.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as UN F ALTERING: UN F, altering, gives FUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfaltering means steady and never wavering, going on without pause.

clue.text: Man appearing in ring and gold tiara, looking strange

indicators.note: looking strange suggests the letters of the words before have been rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone in a boxing ring wearing a gold tiara looks odd.
explanation.walkthrough: The ring is an arena, not a boxing ring or a piece of jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A gladiator was a man who fought in the Roman arena, a ring for combat.

clue.text: Scots town is very noisy after bar opens

indicators.note: after places the noisy letters behind the bar word

parts.note: to bar is to ban
ff (fortissimo) is the musical mark for very loud

explanation.surface: A Scottish town turns rowdy as soon as the pub opens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opens' says the bar word comes first in the answer; the bar here is a verb, to prohibit, not a pub. BANFF is a town in north-east Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Banff is a small coastal town in Aberdeenshire, Scotland.

clue.text: Plan of South Central railway

indicators.note: central means the middle letters of the word South are kept

parts.note: a railway line

explanation.surface: A map or scheme of a railway company serving the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South Central' reads like a rail franchise name, but Central picks OUT from the middle of SOUTH.
explanation.definitionFit: An outline is a rough plan or sketch of the main features of something.

clue.text: Not right, like a highlander naked before the Queen

indicators.note: before puts the highlander phrase ahead of the queen letters

parts.note: a highlander stripped is out of his kilt
ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A Highland Scot stripped bare in front of the monarch is not proper.
explanation.walkthrough: A kilt is the traditional Scottish Highland skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of kilter means out of balance or not working properly, idiomatically.

clue.text: Oxford college dance Oriel oddly rearranged

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: rearranged says those picked letters are shuffled
oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of Oriel

explanation.surface: Oriel, another Oxford college, oddly reorganised as a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' gives OIL from Oriel, and 'rearranged' turns it into IOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Balliol is one of the oldest colleges of the University of Oxford.

clue.text: Scoring the same is annoying without decider at the end

indicators.note: without says a letter is removed from the annoying word

parts.note: trying means irritating, annoying

indicators.note: at the end picks the final letter of decider

explanation.surface: A drawn match is irritating when there is no decisive tie-break at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decider at the end' looks like a sports tie-break; it is just R, the last letter of decider.
explanation.definitionFit: Tying a match means finishing level, with both sides on equal scores.

clue.text: Demanding attention, meaning to get round little sister

indicators.note: to get round says the meaning word surrounds the sister

parts.note: intent means meaning, purpose
sis is a short form of sister

explanation.surface: Wanting someone to give a younger sister the run-around.
explanation.definitionFit: Insistent describes someone who demands notice, refusing to be ignored.

clue.text: Bring in one from Parisian press to give answers

parts.note: to import goods is to bring them in from abroad
une is French for one, a Parisian's word

explanation.surface: Bringing in someone from the French press to answer questions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' looks like the newspapers; it is the verb, to urge.
explanation.definitionFit: To importune is to pester someone persistently with requests or demands, here for answers.

clue.text: Loving country music group — every year it's over touring clubs

parts.note: pa, per annum, every year
a trio is a group of three musicians

indicators.note: over says the it word is reversed

parts.note: the word it, its letters turned
C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards

explanation.surface: A country music band touring clubs every year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country music' looks like the genre; 'Loving country' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriotic person loves their nation, devoted to the homeland.

clue.text: Initial shock when queen and rook are taken resulting in punch-up

indicators.note: are taken says these letters are captured, removed, from the phrase

parts.note: first means initial
a fright is a shock
R for Regina, queen
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A chess game where the first shock comes as the queen and rook are captured, leading to a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture is a decoy: both R letters are taken from FIRST FRIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A fist fight is a brawl with bare fists, an informal punch-up.

clue.text: Offer it when at fault?

indicators.note: at fault suggests the letters of the words before are wrong, needing rearrangement

explanation.surface: A suggestion to give something up when one is to blame.
explanation.definitionFit: A forfeit is something surrendered as a penalty for a fault.

clue.text: Escorted around Haiti's empty capital

indicators.note: around says the escorted word is turned back to front

parts.note: led means escorted, guided

indicators.note: empty means the inside of Haiti is removed, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone was shown round the deserted capital of Haiti.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks tied to Haiti, but it is the definition of a different capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Delhi is the capital territory of India, home to the national capital New Delhi.

clue.text: Tail went up for something smelling nice in the hedgerow

definitions.text: something smelling nice in the hedgerow

parts.note: to dog someone is to tail them
rose means went up

explanation.surface: A tail rising for something fragrant in a hedge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tail' looks like a noun; it is the verb, to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: The dog rose is a wild rose of hedgerows with scented pink flowers.

clue.text: Accustomed to keep risks ultimately covered

indicators.note: to keep means the accustomed word holds another letter inside

parts.note: inured means hardened or accustomed

indicators.note: ultimately picks the last letter of risks

explanation.surface: Used to keeping one's risks covered in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Being insured means being covered by a policy against loss.

clue.text: Hoe user departs with garden tool

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for departs in timetables
a rake is a garden tool

explanation.surface: A gardener with a hoe goes off with another tool.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hoe is Plymouth Hoe, the seafront where Sir Francis Drake played bowls; the hoe is not a garden tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Francis Drake famously played bowls on Plymouth Hoe before facing the Armada.

clue.text: Approaching the airport wing to wing is never to be introduced

indicators.note: is never to be says the letters named next are struck out of the words before
introduced points to each word's introduction, its opening letter

explanation.surface: A plane approaching an airport flies wing to wing with a craft that must never be shown in.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the first letters of 'wing', 'to' and 'wing' to leave ING, O and ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingoing means coming in, as a plane on its incoming approach to land.

clue.text: Timber tree that's very good, almost smooth on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside says the shortened smooth word wraps around
almost says the smooth word loses its last letter

parts.note: to iron is to smooth
OK means fine, all right

explanation.surface: A wood tree that is excellent, almost smooth on its exterior.
explanation.walkthrough: Iroko is a West African hardwood, sometimes sold as African teak.
explanation.definitionFit: Iroko is a large West African tree yielding hard teak-like wood.

clue.text: New York opera house has no time for melody

parts.note: the first part of the name the Met

indicators.note: has no says a letter is removed from the opera house

parts.note: the Met, the Metropolitan Opera in New York

explanation.surface: A New York opera house has no time for a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the main tune or musical subject of a piece.

clue.text: Nothing on earth would interest one in this subject

definitions.text: Nothing on earth would interest one in this subject

parts.words: Nothing on earth would interest one in this subject
parts.note: a student of the stars and planets studies things beyond our planet, not on earth

explanation.definitionFit: Astronomy is the science of celestial bodies, which lie beyond the earth.

clue.text: Certainly easy to unravel as answer drops out

indicators.note: to unravel says the letters of easy are disentangled and rearranged

explanation.surface: It is surely easy to work out when the answer falls away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops out' says the A for answer leaves EASY before its letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes is the affirmative reply, an emphatic certainly.

clue.text: Contents of wooden box, one not going down with ship

definitions.text: one not going down with ship

indicators.note: contents of means the outer letters of the box word are removed, leaving its inside

parts.note: a crate is a wooden box

explanation.surface: What is in a packing case, a survivor who refuses to sink with the vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Rats proverbially desert a sinking ship, so a rat is one not going down with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rats are said to leave a sinking ship, so the rodent is the one that escapes.

clue.text: Our cheaters could be?

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters of the words before may be rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about whether our cheats might be disloyal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheaters are deceitful and disloyal, the qualities of the treasonous and untrustworthy.
